strings.name: Audrey Tang
strings.role: Software developer · Former digital affairs minister
strings.summary: Born in Taipei, Tang left formal school as a teenager, learned independently and participated in Perl, Haskell and free-software communities before civic technology work with g0v. Tang entered government in 2016 and led the new digital affairs ministry from 2022 to 2024, advancing open collaboration, participation and digital services. Tang coauthored Plurality with Glen Weyl and a community, received the 2025 Right Livelihood Award and continues international discussions of technology and public trust.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; reviewed November 15, 2026. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Contributed to free software and digital public services, advancing open governance, civic technology and forms of public collaboration.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Free software and civic technology
strings.highlights.h1.text: Moved from programming-language communities to g0v, applying open development to public affairs.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Participatory digital governance
strings.highlights.h2.text: Supported public collaboration mechanisms such as vTaiwan, connecting digital tools and democratic decisions.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Joining Columbia policy exchanges
strings.timeline.t1.text: Listed among the 2026–27 Carnegie Distinguished Fellows, discussing technology and democracy.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Right Livelihood Award
strings.timeline.t2.text: Recognized for social uses of digital technology, public empowerment and democratic collaboration.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Plurality and leaving office
strings.timeline.t3.text: Published the collaborative-technology book with Glen Weyl and a community; concluded the digital affairs term that year.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Leading the digital affairs ministry
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became the new ministry’s first minister, serving until May 2024.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Pandemic digital-service collaboration
strings.timeline.t5.text: Government and civic-tech communities collaborated on mask availability tools using open data.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Entering government
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became a minister without portfolio for digital affairs, bringing open collaboration into public administration.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Civic technology practice
strings.timeline.t7.text: Helped digital communication and collaboration during the Sunflower Movement, informing later consensus tools.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Turning to independent learning
strings.timeline.t8.text: Left formal schooling at 14, continuing through the internet and free-software practice.
